document_summary: Day Pitney law-firm alert (July 31, 2026) reporting New Jersey's enactment of the FAIR Act (P.L. 2026, c. 43), which bans algorithmic rent-setting using competitors' nonpublic data, effective July 1, 2027.

rules.title: New Jersey FAIR Act (Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent)
rules.requirement: Residential rental property owners may not use algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rents, and software providers/coordinators may not use such software to facilitate agreements or coordinate pricing among competing landlords.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic rent-setting software using competitors' nonpublic leasing information
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property owners, property managers, and software providers/"coordinators" using algorithmic revenue management software or devices that use nonpublic, competitively sensitive information from multiple residential rental property owners.
rules.exemptions: Does not prohibit spreadsheets requiring human analysis, publicly available rent estimation tools, traditional real estate listing databases, and government-administered affordable housing programs.
rules.interaction: May preempt the Jersey City and Hoboken algorithmic-rent ordinances once effective; this document does not address preemption. Preserves existing remedies under the New Jersey Antitrust Act; attorney general to set up a complaint portal.
rules.quoted_span: The FAIR Act prohibits residential rental property owners from using algorithmic revenue management software that collects or processes competitors' nonpublic leasing information to set or recommend rental prices.
rules.conflict_note: Open question: the FAIR Act may preempt the Jersey City and Hoboken algorithmic-rent ordinances once it takes effect on July 1, 2027. This law-firm alert does not discuss preemption of local ordinances.
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary source (Day Pitney alert dated July 31, 2026). Signed July 20 (2026) by Governor Sherrill; effective date July 1, 2027 per the alert, which is after the query date 2026-10-01, so status is not_yet_effective. Statutory section cite not given beyond P.L. 2026, c. 43.
